identity.defect: Scope.Tx() returns full pgx.Tx whose Begin/Commit/Rollback methods a callback could call, allegedly violating 'callbacks access the transaction only through the narrow scope' and 'callers cannot begin/commit/rollback/retry/nest'

findings.dispositionReason: Counter-evidence: (1) Parent spec #138's Transaction-participation decision defines the scope's content verbatim as 'exposes the active database transaction and permits registration of after-commit effects' — the active database transaction in this stack IS pgx.Tx; a lifecycle-free narrowed interface is not demanded anywhere and its construction ('wrapper interface + migrate audit/users/auth helper signatures') contradicts #138's explicit anti-abstraction decisions ('Do not introduce a Go interface solely for mocking'; 'no Repository, DAO, fake storage port, or test-only production abstraction') and #139's own constraint of an independently shippable prefactor that changes no user-visible behavior. (2) AC2 states lifecycle OWNERSHIP ('唯一 owner') — who performs begin/commit/rollback — which remains exclusively the Runner; grep evidence: zero non-writetx Begin/Commit/Rollback calls anywhere under server/internal/ (verified 2026-08-25). (3) Prior art: the pre-change accepted contract handed callbacks the raw pgx.Tx parameter with identical exposure (ADR-0015 写事务纪律 unchanged by it), and AC7 requires those semantics unchanged. (4) Type-level prevention is unachievable regardless: any SQL-execution capability lets a contract-violating callback issue raw 'COMMIT', and the tx value can outlive Run; the enforcement is the documented contract plus review, as before. The reviewer's failure scenario requires a callback to violate the documented contract — out of scope for what any callback contract can guarantee.
evidence: spec #138 Implementation Decisions — Transaction participation: 'Its callback receives a narrow transaction scope that exposes the active database transaction and permits registration of after-commit effects. Session never starts, commits, rolls back, or retries a transaction.'
